newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African oil controls unconstitutional - retailer.
newsitem.headline: S.African oil controls unconstitutional - retailer.

text.p: Price controls governing the South African oil industry are unconstitutional and may be challenged in the country's highest court, leading retail chain Pick 'n Pay Stores said on Monday.
Strategic and manpower planning director Nicholas Bicket said the company was prepared to take the government to court to end price fixing if it continued to drag its feet over reforms.
"We may be compelled to approach the constitutional court for relief from the state's continuing prevarication in the matter of deregulation," Bicket told the Africa Oil conference.
"We think it is thoroughly unconstituional that we can be told the price at which we should be allowed to sell a commodity."
The company was currently looking for ways to import petrol directly from the European oil market to sell at its own discount stations, he said.
The retailer believes it can mark down the price of a litre of petrol by 20 cents by offering a supermarket branded product through "no-frills" self-service stations.
The price of 93 octane gasoline is currently set at 210 cents a litre via the existing in-bond landed cost pricing formula.
At present, all South African filling stations have pump attendants, and the prospect of cut-price self-service operations has raised fears of thousands of job losses.
Bicket said that any shift to self-service would have to be phased in gradually and Pick 'n Pay would initially probably only operate 50-60 stations out of a national total of 5,000.
Longer-term, however, the experience of Europe showed the huge potential of supermarket gasoline retailing, he said.
In Britain, supermarkets have captured 21 percent of the market from the oil companies while in France they have about 50 percent, he said.
The oil industry was the only consumer sector still subject to government controls, together with financial services, another sector that Pick 'n Pay is looking to break into, Bicket added.
